domain: Religious Law / Ritual Studies / Textual Tradition
topic_summary: Analysis of the rabbinic preservation of Temple sacrifice law (Kodashim) through continuous study for ~1,900 years without performance. The kernel contest centers on whether study-without-performance constitutes genuine occupation of the commitment (study-as-exercise reading) or merely archival preservation of a defunct practice (performance-only reading). This collapses the boundary between exercising a commitment and archiving its symbol.

key_entities: Kodashim (Talmudic order on Temple sacrifice law)
Second Temple (destroyed 70 CE; physical locus of sacrifice performance)
Study practice (continuous textual engagement without ritual performance)
Messianic restoration expectation (theological framework for future Temple)
key_tensions: Study continuity vs performance impossibility (1,900 years of engagement with unperformable law)
Commitment occupation vs symbolic archiving (whether study alone sustains the commitment or merely preserves its memory)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The obligation to maintain sacrificial law as binding divine commandment despite physical impossibility of performance
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Rabbinic interpretive tradition grounded in Sinaitic revelation and chain of transmission (mesorah)

readings.commitment: Study of sacrifice law is itself fulfillment of the commandment; the obligation persists through textual engagement
readings.authority_grounding: Rabbinic hermeneutic (study substitutes for performance; Hosea 14:2 'we will render the bulls of our lips')
readings.expected_structural_delta: Study practice enters beneficiary set as legitimate fulfillment; no victim set (obligation satisfied); low extractiveness (study is accessible)

readings.commitment: Sacrifice obligation requires physical performance; study is preparation for future restoration, not fulfillment
readings.authority_grounding: Literalist reading of Torah commandments (sacrifice requires altar, priesthood, Temple)
readings.expected_structural_delta: Current generation enters victim set (obligation unfulfillable); high extractiveness (guilt without remedy); study is placeholder, not satisfaction

readings.commitment: Sacrifice obligation is suspended (not fulfilled, not violated) pending messianic restoration; study maintains readiness
readings.authority_grounding: Eschatological framework (Temple destruction as divine suspension of the commandment system)
readings.expected_structural_delta: No current victim set (obligation suspended, not active); study is maintenance protocol for future reactivation; moderate extractiveness (readiness burden without guilt)

readings.commitment: Sacrifice law is no longer binding; study preserves cultural memory and textual tradition without normative force
readings.authority_grounding: Reform/secular reading (Temple destruction as historical supersession of sacrificial system)
readings.expected_structural_delta: Obligation exits constraint space entirely; study is cultural practice, not religious obligation; zero extractiveness (no normative claim)

axiom_contradictions.basis: Study-as-performance holds that textual engagement satisfies the divine commandment; performance-only holds that only physical sacrifice satisfies it. No single framework can hold both: accepting one requires rejecting the other's account of what constitutes fulfillment.

Performance-only holds sacrifice remains a binding divine obligation; archival-preservation holds it is no longer normatively binding. No coherent framework can hold both: accepting archival reading requires rejecting the claim that the obligation persists.

Study-as-performance holds study fulfills a binding religious obligation; archival-preservation holds there is no binding obligation to fulfill. No single framework can hold both: one requires normative force, the other denies it.

omegas.description: Karaite Judaism rejects rabbinic authority entirely, reading Torah without Talmudic mediation. Does this constitute a fifth reading (scripturalist-only) or collapse into performance_only? Boundary case for reading distinctness.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) — rabbinic authority as unexamined medium

omegas.description: Christian theology reads Temple sacrifice as superseded by Christ's atonement. Is this a distinct reading of the Jewish kernel or a separate kernel entirely? Cross-tradition boundary case.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) — Christian interpretive tradition absent from extraction

omegas.description: Does intensive Kodashim study impose opportunity costs (time, cognitive resources) that constitute extraction even under study-as-performance reading? Potential hidden victim set.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) — who bears costs of study practice

omegas.description: Secular Zionism revived Hebrew and statehood but not sacrifice. Does this constitute implicit acceptance of archival_preservation reading, or suspension pending future decision? State ideology as unexamined constraint.

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Four readings pass distinctness test: each holds a coherent position on obligation status that no single framework could combine with the others.
